notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

Controller hotkeys. In a game's menu, under Controllers, each controller has
Set hotkeys next to Remap. Set one button or several held together for: open
the pause menu, screenshot, performance overlay, quit, save and load state,
next and previous slot, fast-forward, rewind (held, RetroArch only), reset,
and in PC games and ports with the on-screen keyboard, the keyboards and the
touch buttons. Hotkeys belong to the game they are set in; the row at the
bottom, Use these hotkeys for all, makes them the default for every game of
that system, and a game can still keep its own. They work while the game runs
and the pause menu is closed. Quit and reset ask for a second press, and a
card at the bottom of the screen says what happened, or that the game cannot
do it. Capture makes a good first button, since no emulator uses it; a Capture
tap on its own still swaps the Wii U screens.

Ports get the on-screen keyboards and touch buttons PC games have. Every port
with a game window, Twilight Princess included, has On-screen keyboard: Basic
and Extended in its pause menu, and its own touch buttons.

On the web page, every port with folders on the console has a Files button for
its saves, settings and mods, and Twilight Princess (Dusklight) takes texture
packs and mods: drag a folder, an archive or a .dusk file onto its section.

PC games added on the web page ask where to go: the SD card or the Linux
partition, with the free space of each. Before, only installers asked. A game
on the SD card can move to the Linux partition later, with the button under it.

Fixes: a big folder upload in a Files window no longer stops at "Checking what
is already there" with "Could not reach the console". A PC game that takes a
long time to start, like The Witcher 2, keeps its launch screen instead of
showing the game list while it starts. The automatic save state no longer
pauses a running 3DS game. The web page's PC game actions only take requests
from the page itself, so another website open on your network cannot delete or
move a game.

Tested on one console. Hotkeys were tested in RetroArch, Dolphin, PS2, 3DS,
DraStic, PSP, Wii U and a PC game, not in melonDS. The 3DS fix was tested
through the hotkey's save, which works the same way. Typing into a Twilight
Princess text box with the keyboard, a large texture pack, and moving a PC game
that has saves were not tried.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
